comparator.name: Pedagogical Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official Leiden study product and programme description account for the full 180 EC: 60 EC in the propedeutic first year, 60 EC in the common second year, and a third year consisting of a 20-EC specialisation, 25 EC open elective space and a 15-EC bachelor project. The generic registry target does not name one of the three third-year specialisations. Upbringing and Development is selected as the broad route centred on development in and beyond the family; Education Sciences and Orthopedagogy of Upbringing and Education are more sector-specific routes. The 25-EC elective space is genuine open choice and is represented at group level rather than filled with optional examples. The current study product explicitly documents 2026–27 curriculum replacements and supplies the current module identities and EC weights.

alternatives.concept: A UCR programme combines developmental and clinical psychology, cognition, language, social context, youth vulnerability, psychological assessment, communication and empirical methods to study children’s development, learning and support. It is an academic response through related fields. UCR does not offer Leiden’s dedicated pedagogical-sciences curriculum, practicum, communication-lab progression or child-and-family professional training.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic target names Pedagogical Sciences rather than a third-year specialisation. Leiden offers Education Sciences, Upbringing and Development, and Orthopedagogy of Upbringing and Education. Upbringing and Development retains the programme’s broad child-development and family/upbringing identity across ordinary and vulnerable development without narrowing the route to classroom education or clinical orthopedagogy. This selection was fixed before any UCR course was considered.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest programme already incorporates the available developmental, family/social, clinical, cognitive and research courses. A separate Upbringing and Development or clinical-support alternative would largely rearrange the same psychology and sociology courses and would not meet the four-course substantive-distinctness rule. Education Sciences and digital-media directions lack enough target-specific UCR teaching for defensible separate programmes.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce developmental psychology through brain, behaviour and nature–nurture interaction; UCR is broader than childhood.
Both study cognition and learning; UCR emphasises higher cognitive functions and neuroscience.
Both address neurobiological foundations of development and behaviour.
Both study developmental factors affecting children and adolescents; UCR spans the lifespan.
UCR has no dedicated introductory course in pedagogical science or child rearing.
UCR psychology courses are adjacent but do not teach psychology specifically for educational practice.
Both examine how culture and social environments shape upbringing and education.
UCR has no dedicated introductory education-sciences course.
Both introduce difficulties and clinical perspectives, though UCR covers psychopathology generally rather than child-specific pedagogy.
Both include practice linked to education; UCR’s primary-school rhetoric project is not a pedagogical placement.
Both address assessment and diagnosis, though UCR does not train child-specific pedagogical diagnosticians.
Both consider factors affecting wellbeing and support; UCR is health psychology rather than educational clinical practice.
Both address young people’s development outside the family and responses to vulnerability; UCR focuses on resilience to extremism.
UCR has relevant family and social-context perspectives but no dedicated course on optimal development in the family home.
UCR has no caregiver-guidance or prevention practicum equivalent.
Both introduce empirical research design, evidence assessment and statistics.
Both extend first-year research and quantitative methods; UCR centres experimental psychology.
Both develop advanced research practice; UCR emphasises systematic review and meta-analysis.
Both teach qualitative research design and interviewing.
Leiden requires a second statistics and research-methods unit; UCR’s closest scheduled quantitative methods course is already matched above.
Leiden requires a 15-EC independent bachelor project; UCR’s optional independent-research display is separate from the 24 scheduled courses.
Both support structured academic and professional development, though Leiden’s tutorials are programme-specific.
Both develop foundational communication skills.
Both develop ethical judgement; Leiden also covers legal aspects specific to child rearing and development.
Both develop advanced communication and ethical influence; UCR is persuasive communication rather than a counseling lab.
UCR’s selected courses do not reproduce Leiden’s separately credited critical-thinking and academic-writing unit.
UCR offers general philosophy and ethics but no philosophy-for-educators course equivalent.
UCR does not provide this programme-specific practical field orientation.
UCR has social and clinical perspectives but no dedicated family-factors unit in clinical child and adolescent studies.
UCR has empirical methods but no equivalent pedagogical observation practicum.
This is genuine Leiden open elective space, not a universal external subject requirement.

notes.text: Leiden combines child development, education and upbringing, child-and-family clinical assessment, communication labs, practical education and a pedagogical-sciences bachelor project. UCR can study development, cognition, psychology, sociology, communication and research, including one primary-school communication project. It does not provide a dedicated pedagogical-sciences sequence, supervised pedagogical practice, caregiver guidance or professional child-and-family diagnostic qualification.
